title: Heuristic + Statistical Cohort Interruptor for Canary / A-B Rollouts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a combined heuristic and sequential-statistical cohort interruptor that gates Canary and A/B rollouts based on quality/eval signals and system SLOs. The interruptor should enable fast, explainable automatic holds or rollbacks when either: 1) a heuristic (fixed) threshold is crossed (eg. response_error_rate, user-visible-otrs), or 2) a sequential hypothesis test indicates a statistically-significant regression in one or more quality metrics compared to baseline. It must integrate with traffic routing so we can: hold traffic at cohort boundaries, route to fallback model variant, or fully abort a rollout. Outputs must include rationale and metric provenance so PMs/SEs can act without manual triage.
background: We currently rely on manual checks + a basic health check for staged rollouts. Multiple incidents showed regressions that were visible in eval dashboards only after significant exposure. Prior tickets implemented cohort probes and synthetic probes, but we lack a compact interruptor that combines fast heuristics (eg. error rate spikes) with statistically-grounded decisions for quality deltas across noisy signals.
design_decisions: Use two-tier decision logic: immediate heuristic breach -> fast stop; sequential test (SPRT/ADWIN) -> graceful stop with hysteresis.
Evaluate metrics as independent signals but support configurable composite scoring (weighted sum) per project.
Default metric vector: perceived_quality_score (0-100), median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, model_confidence_entropy, user_error_rate.
Keep policy configuration as declarative YAML per rollout (canary_config -> gate_policy -> thresholds / alpha / beta / min_samples).
Integrate with rollout controller to apply actions: hold, divert X% to fallback, reduce cohort share, full rollback.
Produce an 'explain' blob for each interrupt decision with top contributing metrics and recent deltas to include in alerts/PRs.
Use streaming evals and cohort-level rounding to reduce false positives from small sample sizes; enforce minimum sample count before statistical decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Interruptor hooks into existing rollout controller and can take actions: hold, divert, rollback.
Heuristic rules trigger within 10s for error-rate style signals and generate automated alerts in PagerDuty + Slack channel.
Sequential test implementation produces decisions with configurable false-positive bounds (alpha <= 0.05) and documents sample size assumptions.
Explain provenance blob is attached to any automated action and visible in Console rollout timeline.
Can run offline simulation on historical rollout traces and reproduce >90% of manually-detected regressions with <=10% false positives on held traces.
Unit and integration tests for decision logic, configuration parsing, and failure modes.
implementation_plan: Week 1: API + config schema for gate policies; lightweight library for heuristic rules.
Week 2: Implement sequential-test module (SPRT + optional Bayesian sequential) and tie into eval ingestion stream.
Week 3: Build interruptor service that subscribes to cohort telemetry and evaluates policies; add actions to rollout controller.
Week 4: Instrument explain blob generation, alerts, and Console UI hooks (timeline entry).
Week 5: Run offline replay tests on last 6 months of rollout traces; iterate thresholds with PM/Applied ML.
Week 6: Canary deploy interruptor on internal non-critical rollout, monitor results, and iterate for production launch.
testing_plan: Create synthetic regression scenarios (quality drop by 3-10% at various sample sizes) and verify interruptor stops or slows rollout based on policy.
Replay historical rollouts that produced regressions and verify automated decisions match or improve on manual interventions.
Load test: ensure interruptor can evaluate 1000 concurrent cohort policies without adding >5ms median decision latency.
Chaos scenarios: delayed metrics, missing metrics - interruptor must fail open (do not auto-rollback) unless heuristic critical rules are met.
Security review: ensure explain blob does not leak sensitive prompt or PII; redact per KMS policy.
rollout_strategy: Start with internal test org -> 1% traffic public rollout with observe-only mode (no auto-actions) -> 10% with auto-hold only -> 50% with auto-divert + auto-rollback enabled. Each stage requires sign-off from SRE and PM with defined monitor windows.
metrics_and_alerts: Primary quality metric: perceived_quality_score (eval harness aggregated) - alert if delta <= -1.5 points and p <= 0.05 after min_samples.
Latency SLOs: p95_latency_ms > baseline_p95 * 1.2 triggers heuristic stop.
User-visible errors: error_rate > 0.5% absolute increase triggers immediate hold.
Dashboard: per-cohort stream of metric deltas with running p-values and sample counts.
PagerDuty: actionable interruptor incidents that include explain blob and link to rollout timeline.
open_questions: Which sequential test should be our default across teams? SPRT is fast but requires explicit alt hypothesis; Bayesian sequential is more flexible but harder to explain.
How to parameterize composite scores across diverse workloads? Suggest project-level policy templates and a global default.
What is the minimum sample size and warm-up period for user-facing cohorts to avoid noisy auto-rollbacks?
How do we handle multi-metric tradeoffs (eg. small quality gain but large latency regression)? Recommend a configurable policy weight vector and prioritized hard-stops for safety signals.
